---
title: "Custom tools for insurers and reinsurers"
description: >
  Pricing, reserving, reinsurance and capital tools built around your data, methods and governance.
---

NetSimR and its six tools are free. The same approach — actuarial methods validated against
established packages, in tools that people who do not write R can use — can be built around
your own data, assumptions and processes.

## How the work is done

- **Your data, where it lives**: databases, Excel workbooks or files, read as they are.
- **Your data stays yours**: a tool runs on your own servers or on each actuary's computer, and
  sends nothing outside, as [NetSimR's tools](try-online.html#your-data-stays-on-your-computer) do.
- **Your methods and assumptions**: the tool does what your actuaries do today, faster and the
  same way every time, with the choices they make in it recorded.
- **Validated**: results checked against established packages and hand calculations, with
  automated tests, as NetSimR's are.
- **Documented**: reports that explain the figures to a committee, an auditor or a regulator.
- **Delivered the way you work**: a tool in the browser, on your own servers or on each
  actuary's computer, or an R package for your team, with training and a handover.

## See the tools

The [Try online](try-online.html) page runs NetSimR's six tools in your browser, and its gallery
shows them at work. [A worked example](worked-example.html) runs each tool on example data and
opens the report it writes, the kind of document a custom tool hands to a committee. The vignette
[From pricing to capital and reserves](EndToEnd.html) follows one portfolio through the same
steps in code.

## About the author

Yiannis Parizas (BSc, MSc, FIA, MBA, ACII) wrote NetSimR and its tools. He was editor-in-chief of
*The Actuary*, the magazine of the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries, for two years, after two
years as its general insurance and data science features editor. His articles there include the
three that the package's methods refer to: "Free for all" (2023), "Escaping the triangle" (2019)
and "Taken to excess" (2019). [His articles in The
Actuary](https://www.theactuary.com/authors/yiannis-parizas).
